t: The Delian League was founded in 478 BC on the island of Delos to continue the fight against the Persian Empire after the Battle of Plataea.
Most members chose to pay a tax to the joint treasury rather than supply ships, and Athens used the funds to build up its own navy.
In 454 BC Pericles moved the treasury from Delos to Athens, and tribute paid to the league funded building on the Acropolis, including the Parthenon.
dyk: League members swore to have the same friends and enemies and dropped ingots of iron into the sea to symbolize the permanence of their alliance.
ev: After Sparta withdraws from the war, a congress on Delos founds a new alliance under Athens
Naxos becomes the first member to attempt to secede and is defeated
Thasos defects to Persia and is forced back into the league after more than two years of siege
Athens sends 250 ships to aid the Egyptian revolt of Inaros and Amyrtaeus, an expedition that ends in heavy losses
Pericles moves the league's treasury from Delos to Athens
A peace with Persia, known as the Peace of Callias, is reported, though some writers believe the treaty a later myth
The Peloponnesian War breaks out between the Delian and Peloponnesian Leagues
The league is dissolved at the end of the Peloponnesian War, under the direction of Lysander

f.capital: Delos (congresses and treasury), then Athens (treasury from 454 BC)
f.founder: Athens, at a congress on Delos; Aristides set the members' tax
f.predecessor: The Hellenic alliance that fought Xerxes I's invasion
f.successor: Spartan hegemony; later the Second Athenian League (377 BC)
